# Stock status: FLStockR and MVLN

`ss3stk()` builds a simplified `FLStockR` (as `FLRef::ss2FLStockR()`): SSB, F, recruitment and catch, with the
reference points in `@refpts`. `output = "mle"` gives the maximum likelihood estimates with their standard errors,
`output = "iters"` draws from a multivariate lognormal (MVLN) approximation (`ss3mvln()`):

- `method = "joint"` (default) draws SSB, recruitment and F of all years and the reference points from one MVLN
  with the full correlation matrix of the SS3 derived quantities (Kell et al. 2023; the `ss3om::ssmvln()`
  approach). Each draw is a coherent trajectory and the reference points have draws.
- `method = "annual"` is the delta-MVLN of `ss3diags::SSdeltaMVLN()` (Walter and Winker 2020; Winker et al. 2019),
  drawn year by year from the B ratio, F and the F reference.

```{r stat-stk, fig.height = 6, fig.width = 9}
stk <- ss3stk(ss3sma, output = "iters", iters = 1000, fwd = TRUE)
ss3plot_trj(stk)
```

> **SSdeltaMVLN understates the B-F correlation.** For the example models the year-by-year delta-MVLN gives a
> correlation between B/Bmsy and F/Fmsy in the terminal year of -0.24 for shortfin mako (SS3 covariance: -0.86) and
> -0.26 for Pacific hake (-0.76), so its Kobe clouds are rounder than the estimated uncertainty. The joint method
> keeps the estimated correlation; use it for advice.

## Which targets: the reference point basis

SS3 can report stock status relative to different benchmarks, set in `starter.ss` (the B ratio denominator and the
F report basis) and `forecast.ss` (the benchmarks; the MSY option can be set to the F at a biomass target or at an
SPR target). The SS3 labels of the derived quantities also changed between versions. `ss3stk()` works out the
basis with the logic of `ss3diags::SSdeltaMVLN()` and `SSsettingsBratioF()`:

1. **B ratio**: the SS3 `Bratio` of the end year is compared with SSB relative to SSB virgin, SSB_MSY and SSB_Btgt
   (or SSB at F0.1); the closest defines the B target.
2. **F basis**: from `F_std_basis` (SS 3.30) or `F_report_basis` (3.24): absolute F, F/Fmsy, F/F at the B target,
   or F/F at the SPR target.
3. **F reference**: MSY, unless the MSY benchmark is the B target benchmark (then the F at the B target) or the SPR
   benchmark (then the SPR F); `Fref =` overrides it.

The status values agree with `SSdeltaMVLN()` for all example models and for the SS3 benchmark options. The labels
name the benchmark behind each target rather than the SS3 label, because "MSY" in SS3 output may be a proxy:

| Basis | B target | F target | Catch reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| MSY benchmark | `Bmsy` | `Fmsy` | `MSY` |
| B ratio relative to B0, target fraction 40% | `B40` | (from the F basis) | |
| biomass target 40% (or MSY set to F(B40)) | `B40` | `F40` | `Y40` (yield at B40) when MSY is the proxy |
| SPR target 40% (or MSY set to F(SPR40)) | `Bspr40` | `Fspr40` | `Yspr40` when MSY is the proxy |
| F0.1 | `BF0.1` | `F0.1` | |

The catch reference stays `MSY` when SS3 estimated MSY. The basis is stored in `attr(stk, "basis")`:

```{r stat-basis}
str(attr(ss3stk(ss3sma), "basis")[c("B", "F", "C", "bbasis", "fbasis")])
str(attr(ss3stk(ss3simple), "basis")[c("B", "F", "C", "bbasis", "fbasis")])
```

## Key quantities as FLQuants

```{r stat-flqs}
q <- ss3_flqs(stk, c("SSB", "F", "B/Btgt", "F/Ftgt"))
names(q)
```
